title: God the Shepherd
lead: In the ancient Near East kings were called shepherds of their people. The Bible gives the title to Israel's leaders, judges the bad shepherds among them, and gives it above all to God and to Jesus, the good shepherd.

sections.b: Kings of Babylon, Assyria and Egypt called themselves shepherds, and Israel used the same picture. Moses asked God for a leader so that the people would not be like sheep without a shepherd (Numbers 27:17), and God took David from the sheep to shepherd Israel (2 Samuel 5:2; Psalm 78:70–72). The prophets condemned the shepherds who fed themselves instead of the flock (Jeremiah 23:1–4; Ezekiel 34:1–10).

Jacob blessed "God, my shepherd from my first day until this day" (Genesis 48:15). The Psalms call God the shepherd of Israel (Psalm 80:1) and of one person (Psalm 23:1). Ezekiel promises that God himself will search for his sheep and set one shepherd, "my servant David", over them (Ezekiel 34:11–24). Jesus calls himself the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11–16), and the New Testament calls him the great shepherd and the chief shepherd (Hebrews 13:20; 1 Peter 5:4).
